title: Zanzibar's spice loaders and gold-spiked bank doors
summary: He describes Zanzibar, its cinnamon-colored workers and bank doors with gold spikes against elephants.

blocks.x: No, I just called his name. Well, that thought escapes me. Anyhow, it was his palace -- it will come to me. And you know, Zanzibar is the largest exporter of spices in the world -- the peppers and ginger and cinnamon -- comes from Zanzibar, and the fellows who load those ships -- these bags, they have done it so long til their skin has turned the color of cinnamon -- into the skin and it doesn't wash out. They're a yellowish-brown -- a yellowish-brown, and the head and their shoulders and bodies and through the whole system -- they can't live long. But only certain people do that and they have turned the color of the cinnamon and the powder, they've done it for so long. Another interesting feature in Zanzibar was all the banks have large, mahogany doors with golden spikes on them. So, we inquired what were those spikes about. They said, 'Well, years ago when a guy wanted to break in -- sultan in the sultan's palace or one of his banks -- they just bring the elephant and push the door down and go on in and rob the bank.' So they put big golden spikes on every bank -- there's spikes that protrude at least a foot and a half of solid gold
on the fronts of all banks or any big business store, they put these big spikes to keep the elephants from pushing the doors in. The elephants won't go into those spikes. Fantastic.

And gold too, gold. Zanzibar is quite a place, it's a very romantic place. You know, all writers have written about Zanzibar, especially those sea tales. But we went all the way over there to play for a beauty contest that lasted about an hour and a half and got on our planes and went back to Dar es Salaam.
